items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: Plus I did a lot of listening to George Shearing who is one of my heroes.

ctx.x: Well the thing is you’ve got to know how to follow them, not lead them. One of the main things you do for singers — because most of the singers use the Great American Songbook — I hate to keep saying that but the Great American Songbook is the way of life, as I said before. If Art Tatum and Charlie Parker played it, who are we not to? Bird never wrote any — Bird wrote a couple of blues numbers [scats] and rhythm. Mostly everything that Charlie Parker played was “You and the Night and the Music” and “In the Still…

you’re doing, I’ll meet you at the end you see. So that’s really what I tell young piano players. Some of the greatest piano players I know are the ones the played for singers, like Tommy Flanagan, like Hank Jones, like Oscar Peterson. Oscar Peterson with Billie Holiday, great accompaniment. Oh yeah. Like Ellis Larkins. Like my hometown, who Hank Jones says is probably number one, Jimmy Jones, who did orchestrations for Duke, who played on that famous record with Sarah Vaughan with Clifford Brown or Joe Benjamin…
